messages:
Maya (oncall): :rotating_light: incident-bot fired for latency-p95-eu, automated page. Seeing an uptick starting ~09:02 UTC.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: page fired -> escalation policy: latency-p95-eu. Trigger: p95 latency > 350ms for 3m.
Maya (oncall): acked via PagerDuty. I'm on it, grabbing dashboards.
Maya (oncall): samir are you around to help correlate KV-cache evictions?
Samir: here, on phone. pulling perf graphs. Any customer reports?
Kelly: I haven't seen any support tickets yet but I can watch the support inbox.
Ivan: I'm seeing a spike in p95 at the GPU side, looks like tail latencies from a batch worker queue.
Maya (oncall): logs: `gpu_serving: request_latency p95=410ms p99=890ms host=eu-prod-3`
Samir: check autoscaler events? maybe a scale lag.
Ivan: autoscaler looks stable, no new nodes in last 10m. but backlog of large-seq requests spiked, qlen rose from 20->120.
Maya (oncall): temporary mitigation: reduce max_batch_size to 8 for eu pool to reduce queuing — applying via runtime-config now.
Samir: :+1: rolling the config on eu-prod-* (patch policy). command: `pictl config set runtime.eu.max_batch_size=8 --rollout`
pagerduty: Maya acknowledged the page at 09:04 UTC.
Maya (oncall): applied. watching metrics. qlen falling to 40. p95 dropping to ~270ms.
Ivan: kv-cache eviction rate increased earlier, maybe cache churn due to a burst of long-context requests. If prefix KV misses spike, each request pays warm-up cost.
Samir: suggesting we enable short-term prefix caching for the top routes. Can we whitelist production /completions endpoints?
Maya (oncall): yes, drafting a cache rule now.
Kelly: Ops note: customer-facing degraded messages suppressed for now; no visible error rate increase. We should update status page only if we expect >10% degradation or errors.
Maya (oncall): quick root-cause hypothesis: sudden influx of long-seq batches from a partner integration triggered queueing, leading to p95 burn. The alarm threshold is aggressive (350ms) and hysteresis is minimal, causing autopage on transient bursts.
Ivan: agree. we also see that the p95 window uses 3m, but our batching tail can be bursty for ~4-5m during rollups.
Samir: action items: 1) keep reduced batch size for 15m; 2) add a temporary prefix cache rule; 3) tune alert suppression/hysteresis to require 5m sustained; 4) notify partner to stagger long-seq burst.
Maya (oncall): I'll own 1 & 2. Ivan can you draft the alert change? Samir will reach out to partner.
Ivan: will open a PR to alert rules: increase evaluation window to 5m and add a 2m cooldown before re-paging.
Samir: pinged partner (cc @integration-team) to stagger pushes.
Maya (oncall): p95 now ~210ms, p99 ~580ms. Queue length normalizing.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: page resolved (ack cleared) by Maya at 09:12 UTC.
Kelly: marking internal notes and will hold off public status update.
Maya (oncall): postmortem stub: noisy alert from transient long-seq burst + tight hysteresis. Will write full postmortem if we get repeat. For now tracking as incident-ops-noise-1769991111.
Samir: thanks. leaving follow-up tasks in ticket INF-4312.
Ivan: logging config changes in changelog and alert PR: will request review.
Maya (oncall): handing back to normal oncall. I'll follow up in morning with summary. :white_check_mark:
Kelly: thanks all. :coffee:
